subject: chemistry
topic: Organic chemistry: alcohols, carboxylic acids, esters, fats and soaps

kept.q: Which functional group is present in all carboxylic acids and is responsible for their acidic properties?
kept.explanation: Carboxylic acids all contain the -COOH group. This group can release a proton (H+) from the O-H part, making the compound acidic. The other groups belong to alcohols, aldehydes and esters respectively.
kept.pidgin: All carboxylic acid get -COOH group inside dem. Na dis group dey release H+ make the compound acidic. The other options na for alcohol, aldehyde and ester, no be acid.

kept.q: Complete oxidation of ethanol (C2H5OH, molar mass = 46 g/mol) with an oxidizing agent converts it fully to ethanoic acid (CH3COOH, molar mass = 60 g/mol). If 23 g of pure ethanol is completely oxidized, what mass of ethanoic acid is produced, assuming 100% conversion?
kept.explanation: Moles of ethanol = 23/46 = 0.5 mol. Since one mole of ethanol gives one mole of ethanoic acid, moles of acid = 0.5 mol. Mass of acid = 0.5 x 60 = 30 g.
kept.pidgin: Moles of ethanol = 23/46 = 0.5 mol. One mole ethanol dey give one mole ethanoic acid, so acid na 0.5 mol too. Mass of acid = 0.5 x 60 = 30 g.

kept.q: A housewife in a village with hard water (containing dissolved Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions) notices that ordinary soap forms a sticky scum and does not lather well when used to wash clothes. What is the chemical reason for this observation?
options: Soap reacts with Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions to form insoluble calcium and magnesium stearates
Hard water increases the pH of the soap solution, destroying the soap molecule
Soap molecules evaporate faster in hard water due to higher boiling point
Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions dissolve the hydrocarbon tail of the soap molecule
kept.explanation: Soap is the sodium or potassium salt of a long-chain fatty acid. In hard water, the soluble sodium stearate reacts with Ca2+ and Mg2+ to form insoluble calcium/magnesium stearate, which is the scum. This scum wastes soap and prevents proper lathering.
kept.pidgin: Soap na sodium salt of long chain fatty acid. For hard water, the soap dey react with Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions to form insoluble calcium/magnesium stearate - na dat one be the scum. Dis scum dey waste soap and e no gree lather well.

kept.q: In a laboratory experiment, 1.0 mole of ethanoic acid (CH3COOH) is refluxed with excess ethanol in the presence of a few drops of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid as catalyst to form ethyl ethanoate (molar mass = 88 g/mol). If the esterification reaction proceeds with a 75% yield based on the ethanoic acid used, what mass of ethyl ethanoate is actually obtained?
kept.explanation: From the equation, 1 mole of ethanoic acid reacting completely would give 1 mole (88 g) of ethyl ethanoate as the theoretical yield. Since the actual yield is 75%, mass obtained = 0.75 x 88 = 66 g. This shows that esterification is a reversible reaction that rarely goes to completion.
kept.pidgin: From the equation, 1 mole ethanoic acid go produce 1 mole (88 g) ethyl ethanoate if e complete well well - na dat be theoretical yield. Since na 75% yield dem get, mass wey dem get = 0.75 x 88 = 66 g. Dis show say esterification na reversible reaction wey no dey always complete.
